subject: SIG Q: Clarification needed for KV cache persistence (A.9)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lynxfinance.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: SIG Q: A.9 wording ambiguous re: KV cache persistence

Hi Neha,

Hope you're well. We're working through the SIG and hit an ambiguity on question A.9 ("Do you persist customer data stored in application caches?"). Our security team is specifically worried about in-memory KV caches used by your inference runtime for prompt prefixing and short-term context storage. The SIG text doesn't distinguish between transient in-memory KV caches and longer-lived cache stores. Could you confirm whether Redwood ever persists KV cache content to disk or object storage in Hosted/Dedicated deployments, and whether that would be considered "customer data" for the purposes of the SIG?

For context: we need a definitive yes/no and the rationale we can include in our risk assessment. If you prefer, we can schedule a short call to walk through the architecture.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Security Engineer, Lynx Finance
security@lynxfinance.com

--

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 11:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SIG Q: A.9 wording ambiguous re: KV cache persistence

Hi Samira,

Thanks for flagging this — it's a good question and one we see come up often. Short answer up front: Redwood does not intentionally persist per-request KV cache entries to durable disk/object storage as part of normal inference serving. Our interpretation for the SIG response (A.9) is that ephemeral in-memory KV caches used to accelerate inference are considered non-persistent and therefore not "persisted customer data."

That said, there are two important caveats you should be aware of:
- Observability telemetry: aggregated metrics and anonymized traces (no prompt-level content) may be written to internal logging or metrics backends for SLO/latency tracking. These are aggregated and not customer-specific content.
- Optional audit export: in Private deployments (customer-managed), customers can enable audit logging which may include higher-fidelity request metadata; if a customer configures export to their storage, that is outside Redwood's default host behavior and should be documented as a customer-controlled data flow.

I'm attaching a short draft (SIG_answers_draft_v0.1.pdf) with proposed language for A.9 and a simple diagram of our caching layers. Can we do a quick 20-minute call to confirm we're aligned? I'm available today 2:30-3:30pm ET or Monday morning.

Proposed A.9 answer (draft):
"Redwood's inference runtime uses ephemeral in-memory KV caches to optimize latency. These caches are not persisted to disk or object storage as part of the hosted or dedicated service. Aggregated telemetry (metrics/traces) is recorded for observability and does not contain raw prompt content. In Private/on-prem deployments, audit/export features may be enabled by the customer; export destinations are customer-managed and are outside Redwood's default persistence behavior."

If that aligns with your security team's expectations I'll update the SIG PDF and send over the final answer.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Call notes + finalized SIG language (A.9)

Samira / Lynx team — thanks for taking the call. Quick written summary and the finalized SIG entry attached for your records. Please let me know if you'd like us to paste this directly into your SIG template or submit via the portal.

Call notes (brief):
- We walked through the inference runtime caching tiers: in-process LRU caches (per-worker), node-local shared caches, and optional external cache providers (Redis) when configured by customers.
- Confirmation: by default (Hosted and Dedicated), Redis is not used for customer-specific persistent storage; any node-local caches are in-memory only and not persisted to disk. Crash-dumps are redacted and do not include raw prompt content by default; our incident response team can produce additional redaction artifacts if required.
- Aggregated telemetry: includes token counts, latency histograms, and anonymized request hashes for linking traces; it does NOT include prompt text or raw customer payloads.
- Private/on-prem: customers can enable audit exports and external caches; those are customer-managed behaviors and must be reflected in the SIG as customer-controlled options.

Finalized SIG response (A.9) - recommended wording:
"Redwood uses ephemeral in-memory KV caching within the inference runtime to improve latency. These in-memory caches are not persisted to disk or object storage in Redwood's Hosted or Dedicated services. Aggregated telemetry (e.g., latency/throughput metrics and anonymized trace identifiers) may be recorded for observability but does not contain raw prompt content or unredacted customer inputs. In Private (customer-managed) deployments, customers may enable audit exports or configure external cache backends; persistence in those cases is controlled by the customer and should be considered outside Redwood's default persistence behavior"

Attachments: SIG_Lynx_completed_20251018.pdf, redwood_kv_cache_diagram.png
